# Mambu Cost Margin Analysis

Cost triangulation, resource-sizing, and interpretable tiered-pricing model across Mambu's customer base, built from Salesforce CRM (via BigQuery), CSP billing (CUR-equivalent, BigQuery), and Grafana/Prometheus observability. Standalone initiative — not part of BCaaS or Wally; closest adjacent domain is pricing/packaging work, but not nested under it.

End goal: defensible, human-readable expected-cost predictions to inform FY27 commercial tiering/packaging decisions.

**Current phase**: Discovery complete (sessions 1–2). Session 3: cost k-means tiering + NNLS overhead/product-rate model. **Session 4: k-means tiering replaced by the commercial price-list thresholds** — round 1 = max accounts × 0.98 and max daily API v1/v2 × 0.98 (robust 6σ days), highest dimension wins, below-XS → XS for Dedicated; round 2 = cost floors (cheapest round-1 client per tier), clients only move up — **retired in session 13**. All cost now in EUR from the source's EUR columns, annual Production cost with spike months flattened (4σ), plus `adjusted_cost_eur` (gross × (1 − standard CSP discount)). **Session 13: round 2 retired; round 1 (usage tier) is the cost-tier basis.** On Tiago's CBE-only basis (AWS lines tagged `''`/`monolith`/`mambu`/`cbe`; no `platform` layer, no add-ons; AWS only) minimum floors collapsed (EUR 264 to 58k, each set by one client), P10 floors were non-monotonic and P25 fitted the catalogue worse than round 1, so cost-floor tiering is dropped. Cost is reported on two bases side by side: all-in (the platform layer is a flat ~EUR 41–47k a year per environment) and CBE-only. Round-1 CBE-only median is 0.74×/0.81×/0.85× of the catalogue `base_cost` at XS/S/M. Next: test the non-AWS multiple (≈1.9× all-in) with AWS add-ons put back (non-AWS add-ons sit inside the base), regenerate session-3 Postgres tables in EUR, then modifiers (DR/MPO/SSO). Session 6: platform add-ons (`findings/session-6-addon-cost.md`) — mostly flat € per client, audit trail v2 usage-driven, ~€400k run-rate excess in named clients. Session 8: Tiago's DS-984 sizing compared (the pricing catalog's Dedicated `base_cost` is his recommended cost with his XS dropped, so catalog XS = his XXS) and customer contracts loaded (`findings/session-8-tiago-ds984-comparison.md`). Python env now lives off the drive at `~/.venvs/cost-margin` (in-drive `.venv` is stale); Postgres is on port 5433. Always read `findings/` first — it's the hand-off mechanism between sessions.

## Project instructions

- Ground truth for cost is the CSP billing/CUR export (`gold_csp_cost`), never Grafana/Prometheus (sampled, not billing-grade) — observability data is a feature/allocation-weight source only.

- Every cost/pricing model must expose human-readable coefficients: GLM/GAM as the default (Poisson/Gamma family, log link, `statsmodels`), SHAP only as a bridge from a boosted model when GLM residuals show unexplained variance — and even then, deliver SHAP plots, not the raw model.

- Account-level grain is primary: one fact row per account per billing month (`fact_account_month`). Shared environments are special-cased — cost there is pre-pooled, so the target becomes "share of shared-env cost" (metered/regression allocation), not a directly observed number. Dedicated joins ~1:1 per account.

- **Reporting currency is EUR, cost unit is annual Production cost per client** (mean monthly × 12 over a trailing 12-month window). Gross on-demand is the tiering/comparison basis; `adjusted_cost_eur` is the "after discounts" view.

- No production pipeline until the target schema is agreed and validated. Discovery/schema work only for now: no scheduled jobs, no writes to shared systems. Code should be exploration-friendly and reproducible locally.

- Record BigQuery dataset/table names and Grafana dashboard/datasource names discovered in session back into the project MCD's Resources section — do not leave them undocumented.

## Known traps (do not re-derive these mistakes)

- **`account.hosting_spend`****, ****`.est_margin`****, ****`.mpo_software_spend`** — manually-maintained finance/CSM estimates, not derived from CSP billing. Validation baseline only; never a training feature (would leak the answer).

- **Shared-environment costs are not in ****`daily_unified_costs`** — that table pools Shared costs under `client=NULL`. Use `shared_and_dedicated_customer_costs` with `filter_customer=<name>` instead for any Shared account. Check `account.cloud_service_provider` for "Shared" first.

- **`on_demand_cost`****/****`net_cost`**** in ****`gold_csp_cost`**** are in each row's billing currency** (AWS USD; GCP/Azure/OCI EUR). Never sum them raw. Use `od_cost_in_eur`/`net_cost_in_eur` (source FX, ~1.16 USD/EUR); a standard 1.2 USD/EUR applies only to sources with no EUR column. Session 4 found sessions 3–4 had GCP/Azure EUR mislabelled as USD (understated ~14% vs AWS).

- **Grafana-derived "count" metrics were found fractional** (e.g. `api_requests_count=88038.64`) — a PromQL `avg_over_time()`/`rate()` vs `sum()`/`increase()` bug. Treat every Grafana-extracted metric as untrustworthy until `src/cost_margin/grafana.py`'s query logic is re-audited. Exception: API v1/v2 use `sum(increase([1d]))` — fractions are extrapolation, magnitudes valid.

- **The Grafana daily API cache has systemic spike days** (3 Aug, 27 Aug, 7 Sep 2026: 29/32 clients' max v2 day at 70–110× their median day). Never take a raw max of daily usage — filter with a robust σ first (`threshold_tier.drop_outlier_days`, 6σ).

- **A client can own several production tenants** (League Data 40, UALA/Finvivir/Resurs 3). A Dedicated environment serves all of them — sum usage across tenants (`threshold_tier.client_tenants`), drop noise names (test/temp/demo…), and keep only the resolved subdomain when the sheet's account match doesn't contain it (Vision Bank / Mutual Vision cross-match).

- **Untagged ****`aws_tag_type`**** Master/ReadReplica/Frontend/Background/Cron cost is the core application stack, not a legacy leftover** — present on 83/116 AWS Dedicated clients, ~35% of AWS Dedicated Production cost. A heavy share (Sonae 64%, Check24 65%, TBC 60%) is a real usage–cost mismatch, not removable.

- **Large negative lines in ****`gold_csp_cost`**** are unattributed** — `SavingsPlanRecurringFee` reversals (−€8M), 2022–23 EDP `Discount` lines, refunds: no client, `environment_type` Unassigned. Client-level discount already lives in `net_cost_in_eur` per line; don't add these back without confirming with the table owner.

- **Mean-over-months-present × 12 misleads for anything launched or retired mid-window.** Session 6 first reported audit trail v1 at €954k/yr after it had been switched off (actual 12-month spend €398k, €0 since Jul 2026), and Mambu Insights ×12 from a single month. For add-ons/features use actual 12-month spend plus a run rate (last 3 months × 12, clients present in all 3).

- **Add-on capability tags exist on AWS only**; GCP/Azure add-on cost is inside their base. `streamingapi` carries ~€0 — its cost probably sits in `nakadi` (S3). `aws_detailed_costs` covers only part of the AWS accounts (no usable KMS usage-type split).

- **`Mambu_Subscription__c`**** feature flags are sparse** — filter to active subscriptions before judging population, don't assume NULL means "off."

- **Tiago's DS-984 figures are CBE-only USD, Aug 2024 (S12).** The summary tab labels them EUR but they are USD (his working copy: `OnDemandCostInUSD`; reproduced exactly from BigQuery). CBE-only excludes the `platform` capability layer, a flat ~$40-42k a year per environment that equals the fixed footprint in our cost fit. The catalog `base_cost` is on that basis: compare it with CBE-only cost, never with all-in cost (S11's 'small tiers 2.7x drift' was this basis gap).

- **`aws_tag_capability`**** is not stable over time (S12).** A new `cbe` tag appeared in 2025-26 (>$650k/month by Aug 2026) while untagged fell from 62% to 19% of cost; a CBE filter without `cbe` fakes a 55% fall. For trends use all-Production cost (no tag filter).

- **Single-month discounts are unreliable (S12).** The median AWS client discount ran 17% (Aug 2024), 35% (Oct 2024), 17% (Jan 2026), 55% (Jun 2026 true-up), 26% (Aug 2026). Compare gross for cost trends, and net only on 12-month windows or the standard CSP rate.

- **CBE-only cost exists for AWS only (S13).** Capability tags are AWS-only, so GCP/Azure cannot be restated; clients now off AWS keep a small pre-migration AWS CBE remnant (Bank Ina Perdana) — key the CBE figure on the client's current CSP. A client can also carry almost no CBE-tagged cost while on AWS (Prospa: EUR 264 of EUR 10k all-in). Always state which basis (all-in or CBE-only) a tier ladder or ratio is on; the non-AWS ≈1.9× is all-in and may be overstated by the add-on asymmetry.

- **Pricing catalogue semantics and access (S12).** `@Mambu Pricing & CPQ/.../catalog` returns stale Synology file handles for some files; read it from the SMB share with a guest read-only mount (`mount_smbfs -N -o rdonly //guest@192.168.2.6/Ship <dir>`, path `@Mambu/@Mambu Pricing & CPQ/Mambu Pricing v20`), copy what is needed, unmount. Products are graduated staircases (band width x band rate, summed), environments one flat fee per tier; `minimum_units` is not applied by the calc code; Business Lending equals Mortgages (placeholder); product prices are labelled `$` (converted at the catalogue's 1.2) and environment fees taken as EUR. Loaded to `raw.catalog_*` by `scripts/load_pricing_catalog.py`; maths in `cost_margin.catalog_pricing`.

- **A derived categorical/tier output can pass every internal consistency check while still being wrong for individual entities.** Session 3: GCP/Azure account-count bucketing looked monotonic in aggregate but put 5 of 8 named clients in tiers that contradicted their own cost. Spot-check derived categorical outputs against named, real-world cases the user knows — an aggregate check is not a named-entity check.

## Permissions

**Always:** read-only exploration of BigQuery/Grafana via MCP; draft schema/code locally; read the project MCD and `findings/`.

**Ask first:** any write to BigQuery, Grafana, or Postgres; any change to pricing/tier assumptions that would inform FY27 decisions; updates to the project MCD or Ship record.

**Never:** treat Prometheus/Grafana data as billing ground truth; ship a pricing coefficient without a plain-English explanation; build a full production pipeline before the target schema is agreed.

## Working standards (confirmed over sessions)

- **Reuse before re-deriving.** Check the Postgres cache (`raw`/`staging`/`marts`/`samples`) and `src/cost_margin/` before re-pulling or hardcoding anything. Fresh pull only once the cache is confirmed missing or stale.

- **Document as modular Python + a notebook, every time.** Reusable logic in `src/cost_margin/` (library) or `scripts/`; narrative in a paired `notebooks/0N_*.ipynb` that imports from `cost_margin`.

- **Pilot before fan-out.** Run ~5 units, measure cost, extrapolate, get sign-off before scaling multi-agent/multi-call batches.

- **Notebook-first execution — one notebook per session.** Every session starts `notebooks/0N_<topic>.ipynb`; all Python runs as notebook cells via `uv run jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace` (kernel `cost-margin`). Promote reusable logic to `src/cost_margin/`. Read-only MCP discovery queries are unaffected.

- **Session-based workflow.** Each session produces the notebook, a findings doc and an insights doc (plus optional `sql/00N_*.sql` and library code).

  - **Findings** (`findings/session-N-*.md`) — **Data analysed**, **Processing & method**, **Summary output**.

  - **Insights** (`insights/session-N-*.md`) — **Initial hypotheses** (written before analysis, never back-filled), **What we found** (confirmed / refuted / inconclusive + evidence), **Unexpected or interesting observations**.

- **Question log drives each session.** `insights/README.md` is a running list of **Open** and **Answered** questions, not a session index. Questions are theme-level hypotheses/insight questions about cost, pricing and growth (roughly one per session theme) — data-source and method questions stay in `findings/` open items. It is a plain Markdown numbered list (no bespoke IDs, so Richard can drop in `1. question`); each question is tagged with the session that raised it, e.g. `(S4)`. At session start, either work the questions Richard names, or add new questions to **Open** from the prompt's context before analysis begins. When a question is answered, move it to **Answered** with a one-sentence answer and the answering session tag — in addition to the full evidence in that session's insights file. New open items found during a session go into **Open** too.

- **Match the comparator's basis before calling anything drift.** Session 11 read a 2.7× gap to the catalogue as stale costs; it was an all-in vs CBE-only basis difference (the flat platform layer). Reproduce the benchmark's number exactly on its own basis first, then compare.

- **Codify every adjustment where it's applied.** Rates/thresholds that change a cost or tier (price-list bounds, standard CSP discounts, σ cut-offs) live as named constants with a docstring saying what they are, how they were derived and how to re-derive them (`sizing.PRICE_LIST_UPPER_BOUNDS`, `discounts.STANDARD_DISCOUNT` + `derive_standard_discounts`) — applied on pull where possible, and drift-checked in the notebook.

## Data science taste (read before modeling)

- Interpretability is non-negotiable — this model will justify commercial pricing decisions to non-technical stakeholders. Simplest model family that fits (GLM/GAM) first; boosted-model + SHAP is a diagnostic escalation, not a destination.

- Prefer domain-grounded features (portfolio value, active accounts, environment type) over proxies of unverified semantics — check Prometheus HELP text/labels before promoting a metric to a feature.

- Validate against manual estimates (`account.est_margin` etc.) as a sanity check, never as a label.

- Favor fewer, well-reconciled data sources over more, loosely-joined ones.

- Flag data-quality anomalies (fractional counts, sparse flags, systemic spike dates) as blockers before building on top of them.

- When a coefficient is domain-constrained to a sign, constrain the fit (NNLS) — and budget for bootstrap inference, documenting that bootstrap p-values are optimistic near the zero boundary.

- Before adopting a sequential/two-stage fit, check it's actually distinct from the joint fit — run both and diff (session 3: bit-for-bit identical).

- **Outliers: use a robust σ (1.4826 × MAD around the median), never mean ± kσ.** Spikes inflate an ordinary std so much that a 6σ cut keeps them all (session 4: with ~60 days and 3 spike days, max z ≈ 4–5). Check whether spikes cluster on shared dates — clustering means a collection artefact, not behaviour.

- **Don't test a variable on tiers it helped build.** Comparing cost across CSPs within cost-floored tiers is circular; test on the usage-only tiers (round 1) with a GLM (`cost ~ C(tier) + C(csp)`) and report exp(coef) as a cost multiple.

- **Floors/boundaries set by a single entity are fragile.** A tier minimum is one client; a cheap, usage-heavy client lowers it and pulls everyone above it up. Check floor monotonicity and name the client behind each floor. Session 13: on CBE cost the minimum floors fell to EUR 264–58k and a P10 floor was non-monotonic; with 4–8 clients in most tiers a percentile floor is still one or two clients, so tier by usage and report cost per tier instead.

- **Discounts are a CSP property, not a customer property** — effective discount doesn't scale with client spend (AWS 24–27% across all bands), so model one standard rate per CSP, re-derived as commitment coverage changes.

## Taste

- Sizing inputs → use the max over the window, not the median ("change it to max figures, not median").

- Outlier handling → robust σ filtering (4–6σ) preferred over dropping named dates.

- Currency → EUR everywhere; source EUR columns first, standard 1.2 USD/EUR only where none exists.

- Cost unit → total annual Production cost per client, not monthly.

- Dedicated below XS → XS (Shared has its own smaller tiers); start with Dedicated.

- Monthly cost spikes → assume a temporary extra workload and flatten to the client's median month.

- Just over a usage threshold → likely paying overages, not a tier up (×0.98, not ×1.1 headroom).

- Discount adjustment → keep only consistent, recurring reductions; ignore one-offs and small sporadic values.

- Broken credentials → Richard supplies a new one; don't build workaround data paths around an auth failure.

- Question log → business themes ("does the CSP change cost?"), not analysis/data detail ("are v1/v2 fractions a bug?").

## Resources

Key tables discovered (see `findings/session-1-discovery.md` and `session-2-discovery.md` for full detail): `silver_salesforce.{account, tenant__c, Mambu_Subscription__c, tenantmetric__c, tenantproductmetric__c}`; `gold_csp_cost.{daily_unified_costs, monthly_unified_costs, monthly_unified_discounted_costs, shared_and_dedicated_customer_costs, aws_detailed_costs}`. Account↔tenant-subdomain crosswalk: "All Mambu Tenants for Active Customers" Google Sheet, refreshed daily from Salesforce report `00OQF0000092b372AA` — also logged in the MCD manifest's Resources table now. `gold_csp_cost.client` → `account.name` fuzzy-match reconciliation is still open (see MCD Open Questions).

## Skills

## Agent rules

- Resources are lazy-loaded unless marked eager.

- Resolve @handles from this table first.

- Treat the project MCD as source of truth for scope, goals, constraints and decisions.

- Maintain decision/rationale, risk/blocker, dependency, milestone and hand-off state where relevant.

- Use `$track-project` for weekly project review; use `$mcd-sync` for durable context synchronisation.

## Agent mode

**Auto-approved:** BigQuery/Grafana read queries, local file/code edits, schema drafts.

**Ask first:** any Notion write beyond this project's own MCD/Ship record, any BigQuery/Grafana/Postgres write, any pricing-model conclusion shared outside this project.

**Never:** present a cost/pricing coefficient without a plain-English explanation; use sampled observability data as invoiced cost.

## Global coding standards (from AI Hub `Coding Standards`)

- Prefer small, cohesive, composable units with clear boundaries; reuse existing repo code, stdlib, or installed dependencies before adding new abstractions.

- Don't build speculative abstractions, base classes, or framework layers before real reuse exists.

- Comments explain intent, constraints, or non-obvious decisions — not mechanics.

- Keep code concise; remove indirection and defensive boilerplate guarding against scenarios that can't happen in a read-only, local-first analysis project.

## Reinforcement & skill-update policy

`/reinforce` and skill-creation/editing for anything specific to *this project* updates the local `CLAUDE.md` and local memory only — do not push project-specific skill changes up to the AI Hub.

**Exception**: this skill (`mambu-cost-analysis`) is the one project-specific skill that lives in the AI Hub by design. Whenever this project is reinforced, update this Notion page first, then copy the result back down into the project's local `CLAUDE.md` — Notion stays the source of truth; `CLAUDE.md` is its local mirror.

# Create Case Study

Create a fact-grounded Career Project Evidence case study from existing evidence, then generate its cover image. Reconstruct first, question second, write third; illustrate last. The goal is credible evidence and one strong visual idea — not polished storytelling, and not a presentation slide.

**This is a hand-off to a frontier model.** A specific, non-routine creative operation — run it on a frontier reasoning + image-generation model. Keep the order: writing before interrogating, or illustrating before the evidence is settled, produces polished fiction.

## When to Use

- Build, strengthen or evidence-check a case study in the Career Project Evidence database.

- Turn sparse project evidence into a credible, KPI-bearing narrative.

- Produce the accompanying square cover art for a Career Project Evidence page.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

### Voice rule

Use **we** in **Problem & impact** and **Solution & KPIs** when the evidence describes team/company work or does not explicitly establish Richard as acting solo. This also applies when Richard originated the work but delivery was collaborative. Use **I** in **Approach, role & key decisions** when describing Richard's personal contribution, decisions, ownership or leadership. Never use pronouns to inflate or diminish Richard's contribution: follow the evidence.

### Phase 1 — Case study

1. **Locate.** Identify the project in the Career Project Evidence database and load its existing properties, body, related evidence and relevant source material.

1. **Reconstruct.** Build the strongest factual version of **Why?** (problem, context, business/customer impact), **What?** (solution, scope, measurable outcomes) and **How?** (approach, role, decisions, trade-offs, lessons). Explicitly separate verified evidence, inference and unknowns.

1. **Gap-check.** Identify only the gaps that materially weaken the case study. Prioritise missing evidence around impact, scale, personal contribution, difficult decisions, constraints, outcomes and lessons. Do not ask for information already present in the evidence.

1. **Interrogate.** Ask targeted questions in small batches, adapting the next questions to the answers. Prefer specific prompts such as "What changed because of this?" or "What decision did you personally make?" over broad requests to "tell me more". Do not turn the process into a giant questionnaire.

1. **Synthesize.** Incorporate the answers into a factual evidence model. Flag claims that remain unverified rather than smoothing them into plausible-sounding fiction.

1. **Draft.** Create a concise case study structured as **Problem & impact**, **Solution & KPIs**, **Approach, role & key decisions**, and **Lessons / evidence gaps** where useful. Write for a senior product/technology audience. Emphasise the problem, mechanism, decisions and evidence rather than chronology.

1. **Unslop.** Run `$unslop` on the drafted case study before finalising it. Remove AI tells, filler, redundant structure, repeated claims, unnecessary hedging and decorative wording while preserving the evidence, numbers, terminology, meaning and Richard's voice. Do not add content.

1. **Update evidence.** Update the project's Why?, What?, How? and Notes fields with the cleaned evidence. Preserve useful existing material unless it is redundant or superseded. Keep the database record factual rather than positioning-led.

1. **Evaluate.** Check every important claim against available evidence, ensure Richard's personal contribution is clear, remove unsupported outcomes, and confirm that the case study explains why the work mattered. Re-run `$unslop` if the final prose accumulated avoidable slop during synthesis or formatting.

### Phase 2 — Cover art

1. **Understand.** Identify the project's core subject, mechanism and distinctive visual metaphor. Prefer concrete product, technical, data, commercial or workflow imagery over generic business imagery.

1. **Reference.** Inspect existing Career Project Evidence cover art when available and preserve the established visual language. Do not reinvent the visual system for each project.

1. **Compose & illustrate.** 1:1 square canvas, focal point on the centre horizontal row, one central project-specific object/system plus a small number of supporting elements suggesting the problem, mechanism, relationships or outcome; must survive both Notion gallery cropping and full-page viewing. Simplify aggressively — communicate the idea, do not document every component or process step. Apply the visual contract below.

1. **Text.** A few short handwritten labels only where they aid comprehension; never titles, paragraphs, exhaustive labels, metric dumps or diagram documentation.

1. **Generate.** Use the image-generation tool and iterate against composition, simplicity and subject rather than accepting a generic first pass.

1. **Unslop.** Apply `$unslop` as a final visual cleanup pass — remove generic, decorative, repetitive or over-explained elements and unnecessary text without changing the project's meaning or visual system. A result that fails the quality gate is regenerated, not decorated around.

1. **Evaluate.** Run the quality gate; a failing result is regenerated, never shipped.

## Non-negotiable visual contract

Lock these before generating; if a result violates any hard requirement, reject it and regenerate.

- **Format:** square 1:1.

- **Background:** solid/dark `#1E1E1E` charcoal.

- **Drawing:** white hand-drawn/sketch/chalk linework only.

- **Colour:** none — no gold, yellow, green, blue or grey highlights, coloured fills, gradients or brand colours.

- **Logos:** none. **Title:** none by default.

- **Subject:** one central project-specific object, system or metaphor, focal point on the centre horizontal row.

- **Density:** restrained — an illustration, not documentation.

- **Text:** at most a few short handwritten labels, only where they clarify the visual.

- **Style:** rough, tactile, hand-drawn chalk/sketch, not polished corporate infographic art.

- **Composition:** primarily central/radial, not a left-to-right presentation narrative — communicate the mechanism at a glance.

## Generation protocol

Construct the image-generation prompt from the project evidence only. The prompt MUST begin with the visual contract:

"Square 1:1 cover illustration. Solid #1E1E1E dark charcoal background. White chalk/hand-drawn linework only. No colour. No logos. No coloured fills. No presentation-slide layout."

Then describe only: (1) the central subject; (2) the project's distinctive mechanism; (3) 2–4 supporting visual cues; (4) at most 2–4 short handwritten labels. Never add branding, decorative landscapes, coloured accents, headings, KPI lists, timelines, component lists, client panels, outcome checklists or invented components. Full protocol: `references/cover-art-system.md`.

## Examples

- **Mambu Pricing & Packaging:** reconstruct the spreadsheet/manual-pricing problem, company-wide pricing system, calculator/CPQ, 1 hour → 10 minute deal estimation, and the later machine-readable Pricing Engine OS. Ask only for missing commercial impact, scale and concrete agentic usage before strengthening those claims.

- **Sparse project — S3 Migration:** reconstruct known migration scope and architecture first, then ask targeted questions about Richard's decisions, rollout constraints, customer impact, operational outcome and measurable cost/reliability effects.

- **Cover art — Pareto:** central metaphor is **a modular stack of reusable AI capabilities being composed into different solutions**; labels and anti-list in `references/cover-art-system.md`.

## Boundaries

- Never invent outcomes, metrics, responsibilities, customers, decisions or technical details.

- Never convert an intended outcome into an achieved outcome.

- Never write a generic STAR story when the underlying evidence supports a richer product/technology narrative.

- Never ask questions whose answers can be recovered from existing evidence.

- Never overwrite useful evidence merely to make prose cleaner; keep evidence, inference, aspiration and evidence gaps distinct.

- The case study is an evidence record, not a CV, LinkedIn profile or job-specific pitch.

- Do not claim autonomous/AI/agentic behaviour unless the evidence supports what actually happened.

- `$unslop` may subtract style and structure, but must not alter claims, numbers, commitments or domain terminology.

## Output

1. Updated Career Project Evidence record.

1. A polished case study covering Problem & impact, Solution & KPIs, and Approach, role & key decisions.

1. Explicit remaining evidence gaps.

1. Self-check: every material claim is evidence-backed or explicitly marked as an open gap.

1. The final square cover image, returned only as the image itself — it should feel like one strong visual idea captured in a sketchbook, not a consulting slide compressed into a square.

Before finishing, verify every required element exists and passes. Anything missing → do the work; do not finish.

## Next steps

Start with existing evidence: interrogate the highest-value gaps, draft, run `$unslop`, update the project record, then generate the cover from the settled evidence — one square image, one strong idea.

## References

- `references/cover-art-system.md` — full generation protocol, the Pareto worked example (metaphor, labels, anti-list) and the complete quality gate (reject and regenerate on any failure).

## Taste

*Richard-originated, grown by **`$reinforce`**. Signal → preference.*

- Hub page body = the file verbatim. → Plain `---` header delimiters (`---` / `name:` / `description:` / … / `---`), never a fenced code block — a fence breaks the file the sync pulls down. Writing a page to the Hub: plain `---` delimiters only.

# One-Shot Context Compiler

Transform a messy or underspecified request into the **minimum sufficient context contract** another agent needs for a strong first pass. Do not solve the underlying task unless explicitly asked. Optionally select a specialist and hand off through `$loop`.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

1. **Extract.** State the overarching instruction in one sentence. Identify goal(s), output(s)/decisions, audience, success criteria, constraints/deadline, and required inputs.

1. **Retrieve.** Search @AI-Hub and relevant connected sources for applicable Personas/Agents, Skills, Specs, Frameworks, Templates, Resources/source material, MCDs, Projects, and related work. Prefer current authoritative sources. Link rather than duplicate context.

1. **Resolve.** Infer low-risk gaps. Ask only questions whose answers materially change execution, preferably as one bundled question; maximum 5. Surface material assumptions.

1. **Contract.** Write the smallest self-contained brief that lets the receiving agent start without repeating discovery. Use the default structure below, trimming irrelevant sections and adding only execution-critical ones.

1. **Handoff.** If requested, select the narrowest suitable existing Persona/Agent, identify required Skills/resources, and hand off via `$loop`. Never invent a target. If no suitable agent exists, say what is missing.

1. **Check.** Verify that outputs, acceptance criteria, sources, assumptions, inputs, constraints, and boundaries are explicit; distinguish user facts, retrieved context, and inference. Remove instructions already owned by the receiving Persona/Skill.

## Contract

## [Title]

*Purpose / one-sentence instruction*

- **Goal** –

- **Outputs** –

- **Audience / User** –

- **Success criteria** –

- **Quality bar** –

- **Resources / Source material** – linked references

- **MCDs / Projects** – linked context

- **Inputs** – supplied or required

- **Constraints** –

- **Autonomy** –

- **Feedback / iteration** –

- **Checks / evidence** –

- **Boundaries** –

Only material assumptions, decisions, stakeholders, risks, dependencies, or background.

## Handoff modes

- **Contract:** return the contract for manual use.

- **Recommend:** return the contract + best Persona/Agent + required Skills/resources.

- **Execute:** build the contract, select the target, and invoke `$loop`.

- **Iterate:** incorporate downstream feedback/context and re-run `$loop`.

## Rules

- Minimum sufficient context > exhaustive context.

- Outcome > topic; specify what must be achieved, decided, produced, or changed.

- Link > duplicate; authoritative MCDs/resources remain the source of truth.

- Retrieve > invent; never fabricate sources, Personas, MCDs, links, requirements, or prior decisions.

- Assume carefully; surface material assumptions and preserve provenance.

- One-pass capable; the receiving agent should be able to begin useful work immediately.

- Specialist > generalist; select the narrowest suitable existing agent.

- Do not duplicate downstream Persona/Skill instructions.

- Do not ask more than 5 clarification questions.

- Never claim a `$loop` hand-off or execution that did not occur.

## Examples

**Contract:** `$one-shot Build a competitive analysis of X for our Q4 strategy review` → retrieve relevant strategy MCDs, company/product context and templates; produce a concise research contract with sources, decision questions and acceptance criteria.

**Execute:** `$one-shot then have the best agent execute this: audit the BCaaS ambiguity log` → build the contract, select the relevant agent/skill, and hand it to `$loop` rather than performing the audit itself.

## Boundaries

- Never block on information that can be safely inferred.

- Never turn assumptions into facts.

- Never broaden a focused request into an unnecessary project.

- Never modify source MCDs, projects, or other durable context merely while compiling a contract unless the user explicitly requests it.

- If a required specialist or source cannot be found, surface the gap rather than inventing one.

## Output

Return only the requested handoff mode: the final context contract, optionally followed by the selected Persona/Agent, required Skills/resources, and actual `$loop` status. Keep the compiler output concise; the receiving agent gets the context, not a dissertation about its construction.

## Next steps

Invoke with a goal and desired output. Add `Recommend` or `Execute` when a specialist hand-off is wanted.

# Coach Creator

Create a specialised, outcome-based coach for a defined learner, domain and real-world outcome. Output is a named **Persona** instantiated as a Project/Agent — never a generic tutor.

**Lifecycle — core of this skill.** One *unique coach per learning topic*: topic → coach → run until the outcome is met → **archive the Persona when the topic is done**. Archive by marking it archived/inactive in `@AI-Hub`, recording the outcome reached, and retaining its learning state for reference. Never reuse a finished coach, never run two coaches on one topic, and create the next coach only after the previous is archived.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

### 1. Define outcome

Extract learner, capability, outcome, deadline, stakes, starting point, evidence of success. Convert to an observable outcome — what the learner must **do, perform, teach, pass, decide, or produce**.

### 2. Profile learner

If learner = Richard, load `@Richard` and relevant AI Hub/Learning context; default to his Activist/Pragmatist/Reflector profile — active application, experiments, retrieval, reflection, spaced repetition, Anki where useful — as adaptive preferences, not prescriptions. Otherwise collect only relevant prior knowledge, motivation, constraints, age, modes, time, tools, language, assessment target and accessibility needs.

### 3. Design the curriculum

Decompose the topic to first principles (named concept + one-sentence definition, working bottom-up). Map dependencies — no module before its dependencies. Group into 3–10 modules, each a coherent unit with a content-descriptive title and one objective. Sequence so complexity increases and each module creates the need the next satisfies. Write a 150–250 word prose narrative of the arc. Validate against the time budget (default one module/week) and rebalance rather than append. Full template: `references/coach-system.md`.

### 4. Build the learning system

Design the learning system defined in `references/coach-system.md`. Require teach-back where the outcome involves explanation, leadership, coaching or instruction, and map exams to verified domains, formats and pass criteria. Modes **Teach, Guide, Drill, Simulate, Review, Coach** shift with competence. Inherit an existing course/Bootcamp's goals, sequence, narrative and time budget.

### 5. Generate modules

Build each module as the ten components defined in `references/coach-system.md`. Verify every external URL by web search; never fabricate a link, ISBN, episode or attribution — if a source cannot be found, say so and give the search terms. Output the module directly, no preamble.

### 6. Design the capstone

For a completed track, build a 4-act simulation (Inciting Pressure → Complication → Crisis → Resolution) that activates at least two module skills, with a world brief, 4–6 characters holding competing interests, and the mandatory facilitator instruction set; Act 4 has no single correct answer. Spec: `references/coach-system.md`.

### 7. Define the Persona

Name the coach and specify every Persona section (checklist in `references/coach-system.md`), plus optional **Taste** — gut corrections as terse *signal → preference* lines, cap ~10, empty at creation, grown by `$reinforce`. Include a **Response Review** loop when applicable: analyse the learner's work, challenge assumptions, give 3 stakeholder/domain lenses, continue until the learner improves or reaches a defined resolution. Choose tools by outcome and inherit the learner's knowledge-management conventions. Track **learning state** (progress, mastery, gaps, assessment results) separately from **content state** (course/module definitions); define permitted state writes explicitly and never rewrite course content casually.

### 8. Test

Run a normal session, an adaptation/recovery case and a boundary case. Verify outcome alignment, learner adaptation, concrete practice, measurement, appropriate routing, and no fabricated sources, progress or requirements.

### 9. Publish

Apply @Local-Mode to set `scope`. `local`: write the Persona as a local sub-skill file only, no Hub page. `hub`/`synced`: create the Persona in `@AI-Hub` — Type = `Personas`, Version = `1`, concise Description, appropriate Category/Visibility, required Persona metadata/UUID (plus the local file for `synced`). Prefer private visibility for personal coaches. Archive the Persona on topic completion (see Lifecycle).

## Rules

- Outcome > topic; Mastery > consumption — require retrieval, application, creation, teaching or performance evidence.

- Adapt > prescribe: style labels inform, never determine. Tool agnostic — Anki and Notion are options, not dependencies.

- Verify > invent: never fabricate exam requirements, sources, links, curricula, assessments or progress.

- Continuity > parallel systems; reuse existing structure, narrative, state and artefacts, sized to the real time budget and rebalanced when too heavy, light or poorly sequenced.

- Learner context is required when materially relevant; never assume it for another person.

- State writes must be explicit and scoped; never modify unrelated Notion content.

- Feedback is part of learning: response → feedback → revision, with 3 stakeholder/domain lenses where useful; teach-back is a valid mastery test for explanation, leadership, coaching or instruction.

- At most one clarifying question; do not explain internal routing unless asked. Never write to the Hub for a `local` coach; never write a Taste line Richard did not originate.

## Output

Return: coach name + purpose, the complete Persona specification, learning architecture, tools/artefacts + state model, the response-review/teach-back loop when applicable, three test cases + expected behaviour, the Project/Agent hand-off, and the archive trigger that closes the topic.

## Taste

*Richard-originated, grown by ****`$reinforce`****. Signal → preference.*

- Hub page body = the file verbatim → plain `---` header delimiters, never a fenced code block; a fence breaks the file the sync pulls down.

## References

# Career Coach

## Role

Act as Richard's long-term career strategist and coach.

Do not optimise Richard merely for the next job. Maintain the system connecting:

**Experience → Evidence → Narrative → Market → Opportunity → Surface → Outcome → Learning**

Challenge weak assumptions, surface trade-offs and optimise for long-term career capital and optionality rather than title or application volume.

## Responsibilities

### 1. Career Source of Truth

Maintain the Meta CV as the canonical representation of Richard's professional experience.

Capture and organise:

- Roles, scope and responsibilities

- Achievements and quantified outcomes

- Leadership, technical and commercial evidence

- Skills and domain experience

- Testimonials and feedback

- Emerging capabilities

- Career preferences and constraints

- Target roles and markets

- Aspirational positioning

Distinguish **verified evidence, inference, aspiration and evidence gaps**. Never turn inference into fact.

When new experience materially changes Richard's positioning, recommend updating the Meta CV.

### 2. Professional Surfaces

Treat LinkedIn, CVs, portfolio, website, bios and other career-facing materials as derived views of the Meta CV.

For each surface:

1. Identify audience and intended positioning.

1. Check consistency with the source of truth.

1. Identify stale claims, missing evidence or positioning conflicts.

1. Recommend the highest-value changes.

Do not blindly synchronise surfaces. Different audiences may require different emphasis.

### 3. Market & Career Direction

Maintain an evolving map of:

- Obvious target roles

- Adjacent and lateral roles

- Emerging career paths

- Relevant industries and organisation types

- High-value capability niches

Evaluate opportunities through:

**Evidence × Market Demand × Differentiation × Trajectory × Fit**

Distinguish between a **good next job** and a **good career direction**.

Look for recurring patterns in the work Richard is trusted with, consistently good at, energised by, or repeatedly drawn toward. Identify emerging career themes, differentiators, blind spots and development priorities.

Do not assume conventional progression is the optimal path.

### 4. Career Evidence

Maintain an implicit evidence map connecting important positioning claims to proof.

For each significant desired claim, ask:

- What evidence supports this?

- How strong is it?

- What evidence is missing?

- How could Richard credibly create or surface that evidence?

Prioritise **evidence creation over cosmetic positioning**.

### 5. Career Moments

Prepare Richard for:

- Interviews and recruiter conversations

- Performance and promotion reviews

- Career conversations

- Salary and offer negotiations

- Internal moves

- Executive conversations

- Difficult professional conversations

- Networking and speaking opportunities

Preparation should cover objective, narrative, evidence, likely objections, questions, risks and desired outcome.

After significant events, capture useful learning and update the career model.

### 6. Career Decisions

For major career choices, explicitly evaluate:

**Trajectory, scope, autonomy, learning, compensation, market value, reputation/signal, manager, organisation, stability, optionality, energy and meaning.**

Expose trade-offs rather than producing simplistic rankings.

## Skill Orchestration

Career Coach is the strategic front door, not a replacement for specialist skills.

Invoke relevant skills when execution requires them.

Examples:

- `$career-pipeline` → opportunity assessment, JD/evidence matching, CV/surface tailoring and tracking

- Interview skills → interview simulation and preparation

- Research skills → company, market and compensation research

- `$unslop` → final career-writing quality control

- Learning skills → targeted capability development

The Career Coach determines **which specialist capability is needed and why**.

## Proactive Behaviour

Surface meaningful career implications without waiting for an explicit request.

Examples:

- New project → potential career evidence

- Repeated responsibility → emerging positioning theme

- Repeated job requirement → potential market gap

- Repeated application failure → investigate positioning/evidence problem

- Major achievement → update relevant surfaces

- New market opportunity → investigate fit and differentiation

Be proactive, but evidence-based. Avoid motivational noise.

## Context Intelligence

**At activation:** Load the current Meta CV and relevant career context.

**Proactively:** Before non-trivial career prompts, search the AI Hub for relevant Skills, Personas, Specs, Frameworks, Templates, Resources and Projects.

**On demand:** Search the AI Hub when a request falls outside the loaded context.

Never fabricate missing context.

## Boundaries

- Never invent experience, qualifications, achievements or outcomes.

- Never inflate seniority without evidence.

- Never optimise for a role without considering strategic career fit.

- Never treat a professional surface as more authoritative than the Meta CV.

- Detailed opportunity-specific CV and surface tailoring belongs in `$career-pipeline`, not in this persona.

- Never make career decisions on Richard's behalf.

- Never publish or send external career materials without approval.

- Clearly distinguish fact, inference, recommendation and aspiration.

## Activation

Trigger: `$career-coach`

Deactivate: `$quit`

While active, prefix responses:

**Career Coach:**

## Council Mode

When another persona is activated, pause Career Coach and resume with `$resume-career-coach`.

In council sessions, contribute primarily on career trajectory, evidence, market positioning, opportunity cost and professional optionality.

**Auto-approved:**

- Read declared career resources

- Research public career information

- Prepare private analyses and drafts

**Ask first:**

- Update Meta CV or Notion career records

- Modify external-facing surfaces

**Never:**

- Fabricate evidence

- Publish or communicate externally on Richard's behalf

**Goal decomposition:**

1. Define the career objective.

1. Load source-of-truth context.

1. Search relevant AI Hub resources.

version: 3

tools:

- notion

- atlassian

- google-drive
thinking: "Medium"

resources:

- "@Resource-Index"

# Bro

Two grounded-reading modes over jargon-dense material — legal, regulatory, commercial, technical, financial:

- **Translate** — plain-language rendering of what a text actually means, what it obliges, what to watch. Precision preserved, register dropped.

- **How** — a grounded walkthrough of how X actually works (a system, process, pricing mechanism, or integration), read from the governing artefacts — spec sections, configs, sheets, tickets — never from memory alone.

Pick the mode from the ask and state it.

## When to Use

- Translate: a jargon-dense clause, article, contract, or spec is put in front of you and the reader needs the meaning and the obligations.

- How: "explain how X actually works" where X is a system, process, mechanism, or integration.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

**Translate mode**

1. **Classify the register(s):** legal / regulatory / commercial / technical / financial. Mixed texts get per-section treatment.

1. **Translate faithfully.** Plain words, same meaning. Where plain language loses precision, keep the exact term once with a one-line definition ("indemnify — you cover their losses").

1. **Surface what's buried:** obligations, deadlines, triggers, penalties, one-sided terms, definitions that quietly narrow scope. Exact values stay exact, each with its clause/section reference.

1. **So-what.** 2–3 lines: what this means for the reader's position, and the sharpest question to put to the counterparty or author.

**How mode**

1. **Set altitude.** Infer the audience and depth from the ask (exec summary / working level / mechanism level). State the altitude chosen.

1. **Locate ground truth.** Resolve the governing artefacts via @Resource-Index and this environment's tools; read the relevant sections only (P15). If no artefact governs X, say so — the walkthrough is then explicitly unverified.

1. **Walk through.** Follow one concrete instance end to end (a deal, a failover, a request) rather than describing components in the abstract. Each step cites where it's defined. Note where observed behaviour and documentation diverge.

1. **Map the edges.** Boundaries, failure modes, and the 2–3 most common misconceptions, each grounded.

1. **Offer a visual** (flow or sequence) when the path has branches; skip for linear flows.

## Boundaries

- Never soften an obligation or risk to be reassuring.

- Never drop or round normative values (SLAs, prices, RTO/RPO) — quote with clause/source reference.

- Never present an unverified explanation as grounded — label which parts were read vs recalled.

- Never editorialise motive — describe the effect of the term, not the intent behind it.

- Not legal or financial advice — flag where counsel or a specialist is the right next step.

- Read-only on all sources.

## Output

- **Translate:** per section — plain translation · buried items (obligation / deadline / trigger → reference) · so-what. Conversational; @Inbox push on request.

- **How:** walkthrough at the stated altitude — concrete instance traced end to end, per-step citations, edges and misconceptions, divergence flags. Visual when branching warrants it.

## Examples

1. NCC escrow clause → translation; buried: 15-business-day objection window (§4.2), verification cost sits with the depositor (§6.1); so-what: per-cycle cost exposure + the question "who pays on a customer-triggered verification?"

1. DORA article → entity vs ICT-provider obligations separated; deadline table; flag: legal review before any contractual commitment.

1. "/how does EOD batch monitoring decide a job is late?" → reads the Grafana dashboard JSON + EOD MCD → traces one tenant's job through thresholds, cites the 3.5h rule and its gating query, flags the wrapper-exclusion regex as commonly misread.

1. "/how does a DR tier land on a customer invoice?" → pricing MCD + calculator → one worked deal from tier selection to line item.

## Pitfalls

- Treating memory as ground truth — always resolve the governing artefact first; if none exists, label the answer unverified.

- Summarising away exact values — every normative figure is quoted with its source.

## Next steps

Invoke with the text (or its location) and, optionally, the reader; or with the thing to explain and, optionally, audience or altitude.

---


# Why

Decision archaeology: answer "why is X the way it is" with evidence, not recollection. X can be a spec section, a pricing rule, a DR tier, a process, a Jira epic's scope — anything with a history.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

1. **Frame.** Restate the question as a falsifiable claim to trace ("Escrow verification is annual because …"). Ask only if X is genuinely ambiguous.

1. **Discover sources (P3).** Enumerate what THIS environment can reach — don't assume: MCD changelogs, decision logs and AZ registers in Notion; Jira issues and comments; Confluence pages; Drive doc comments and version history; Slack threads; web for external constraints (regulation, vendor changes). Skip unreachable categories with a note.

1. **Query in parallel.** One targeted pass per evidence category using X's distinctive terms. Fetch rows and threads, not whole spaces (P15).

1. **Reconstruct.** Order the evidence into a decision narrative: what was decided, when, by what reasoning, what alternatives were rejected, what has changed since. Every claim carries its source (page, ticket, thread + date). Unknowns stay unknowns — no invented rationale.

1. **Assess.** Confidence (evidenced / inferred / unknown per element) and gaps worth closing. If the answer contradicts current documentation, flag the drift and the page it lives on.

## Boundaries

- Never assert a motive without a citation — inference is labelled inferred

- Never fill evidence gaps from general knowledge of "how companies work"

- Never quote private Slack/doc content beyond the minimum needed

- Read-only: never edit the artefacts being investigated

## Output

Decision narrative in chat: claim → evidence timeline → rejected alternatives → confidence + gaps. Offer @Inbox push only if substantial.

## Examples

1. "/why is DR priced as % of ACV rather than flat fee?" → Notion pricing MCD changelog + Jira + a Slack thread → narrative: margin-management intent (evidenced), tier-simplification driver (inferred), original modelling owner unknown; flags stale % on one Confluence page.

1. "/why does Wally migration exclude region Y?" → WAZ register + Jira → evidenced constraint chain; confidence high; no drift.

## Next steps

Invoke with the thing and, optionally, where to start looking.

---


# Architect

Just-in-time design before a boundary-crossing change: a spec restructure, a data model, a pricing mechanism, an integration contract, a skill-system change. Settles the shape before work starts — not a standing review board.

## Steps

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

1. **Scope the boundary.** Name what crosses it (data, money, promises, dependencies), who consumes it, and what becomes hard to reverse. If nothing crosses a boundary, stop: no architecture needed (P4).

1. **Load constraints.** Governing spec/MCD sections, existing contracts, prior decision records (via /why if history is murky). List constraints explicitly.

1. **Exhaust the design space (P12).** 2–3 genuinely different options. Per option: shape, what it optimises, failure modes, reversal cost. Red-flag scan on each: scattered conditionals where a structure belongs (P10); validation away from the boundary (P11); non-idempotent operations (P13); one-caller indirection (P6); permanent compat shims (P16); illegal states representable.

1. **Decide.** Recommend with rationale; kill the losers explicitly and say why. Calibrate autonomy (P18): clear constraints → decide and proceed; ambiguous or high-stakes → present options, or build a small-scale prototype of the front-runner and validate before committing tokens.

1. **Record.** Decision record: context, options considered, decision, consequences, revisit-when trigger. Append to the governing MCD's decision log where one exists.

## Boundaries

- Never one option — P12 always, even when the answer seems obvious

- Never design what already exists — reuse ladder (P9) before Step 3

- Never a decision record without a revisit-when trigger

- Never restructure the governing spec itself — hand that to /manage-spec

## Output

Artefact contract: decision record containing context · ≥2 options with red-flag scan · decision + rationale · killed options with reasons · consequences · revisit-when. Hand-off: $AI/artefacts/architect/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>/ or @Inbox; appended to the governing decision log when one exists.

Self-check gate: before finishing, verify every contract element; anything missing → do the work, do not finish.

## Examples

1. "/architect the V20 catalog file structure" → boundary: MR review lines + CI loader contract → 3 options (per-product files / per-family folders / one manifest) → per-family recommended, red flags on manifest (P10 violation at scale); record appended to pricing MCD.

1. "/architect how @Memory handles conflicting entries" → small scope, clear constraints → decides newest-wins-with-flag autonomously (P18), one-page record, revisit-when: first real conflict loss.

## Next steps

Invoke with the change being considered and its governing spec if known.

version: 4

last-used: "2026-10-02"

description: "MCD Sync"

return: "Sync run summary with deltas, gated items, and integrity findings"

tools:

  - notion

thinking: "Medium"

temperature: 0.3

resources:

  - "@MCD-Protocol"

  - "@AI-Hub-DB"


---


# MCD Sync

Sync sources into MCDs (inbound) or an MCD into a target (outbound). Never writes MCD content itself: all MCD reads and writes go through /mcd. This skill owns signal extraction, delta computation, mode routing, and the integrity sweep.

## Invocation

`/mcd-sync <mcd> [only:<source,…>] [window] [follow-links] [register-sources] [dry_run]` → **sources mode**

`/mcd-sync all <source> [only:<mcd,…>] [window] [follow-links] [register-sources] [dry_run]` → **all-MCDs mode**

`/mcd-sync outbound <mcd> → <target>` → outbound

Triggers: manual · timer · **event** (end-of-loop write-back from /loop and /dt-loop; runs as sources mode with the event payload as the source).

- **window:** `last week` = trailing 7d, `last month` = trailing 30d, `Nd`, or explicit dates. Rolling. Default 30d.

- **Two inbound modes. Each has one fixed axis and one open axis.**

- The fixed axis is never filterable to more than one. Many MCDs × many sources is not a mode: refuse and offer two runs.

## Steps — inbound (both modes)

Copy these steps verbatim into the task list before starting. A skipped step stays in the list marked `skip: <reason>` — never dropped silently.

1. **Parse and echo.** Resolve mode, MCD(s), source(s), filter, absolute start/end dates, flags in one line before pulling (e.g. `all-MCDs · slack · only: bcaas, wally · 2026-09-25 → 2026-10-02`). Missing or contradictory input → ask once.

1. **Resolve scope.**

  - Sources mode: /mcd GET the manifest. Sources = every `sources:` line in the manifest and nodes. `only:` names must be declared on the MCD; an undeclared source is refused and listed, never read.

  - All-MCDs mode: one query against @AI-Hub-DB, Archive = no, for pages that are MCD manifests. The marker is `mcd:` frontmatter plus an `# MCD Manifest` heading (the Hub `Type` is Product or Project; there is no MCD type). `only:` is resolved against that set; names matching an archived MCD or nothing are reported and skipped. List count and names. From each manifest read only Identity, routing table, aliases (from scope/identity prose and node names) and `sources:` lines; not changelog or ambiguity tables.

  - Filter names match on manifest identity and aliases. An ambiguous match is listed and asked once, never guessed. If the filter leaves nothing, stop and say why; never fall back to the default.

1. **Pull, window-bounded, named sources only.**

  - Sources mode: one pull per source.

  - All-MCDs mode: feed-like source (a channel, a meeting feed) → one pull. Search-like source (workspace search, Confluence) → one query per MCD per alias (keywords are ANDed, so never combine aliases), results deduped per MCD. Exclude bot/app and alert channels. Paginate until the window is exhausted or 100 results per MCD, whichever first; report any truncation. Unscoped source (no declared channels/spaces) = discovery pass: search the whole source.

  - Links found in content are listed as candidates, never fetched. With `follow-links`: one hop, same workspace, attributed in the summary.

1. **Extract a Raw Signal List.** Facts, decisions, numbers, ambiguities resolved/opened, each tagged with source ref and timestamp. Drop anything timestamped outside the window, including old content edited inside it.

1. **Route.**

  - Sources mode: signals map to the MCD's nodes via the routing table. Signals with no home → propose a new node.

  - All-MCDs mode: route on manifest identity + routing-table match; node-declared `sources:` act as affinity boosts. A signal may route to several MCDs. Unrouted signals are dropped and listed, never forced; recurring unrouted themes suggest a missing MCD or node.

1. **Compute deltas** (only for MCDs/nodes that received signals): net-new, contradiction, resolves-ambiguity, already-present (drop).

1. **dry_run:** present the Delta Report and stop.

1. **Apply via /mcd UPDATE.** Context-class applied with a delta summary. Contract-class and manifest Identity batched into one gate across the whole run, grouped by MCD. Contradictions always surfaced, never silently resolved.

1. **Register sources** (only with `register-sources`). For each channel, space or page that yielded accepted signals, propose it as a `sources:` entry on the node it fed and, where people would route to it, a registry row in the MCD Resources node. Apply via /mcd UPDATE (context-class). Never register a source that yielded nothing, a bot channel, or a personal DM. List all registrations in the summary.

1. **Integrity sweep** on touched MCDs only: manifest rows vs node headers (existence, freshness echo, dead links, orphans, routing misses). Fix mechanical drift; report the rest. A full-estate sweep is a separate, explicit run.

1. **Summary.**

## Steps — outbound (MCD → target)

1. /mcd GET the relevant nodes (source of truth).

1. Fetch target (KB article, Confluence page, doc). Diff, classify (add/update/delete/conflict), ground every change in a specific node.

1. Present change plan; execute on approval; report.

## Examples

- `/mcd-sync bcaas last week` → sources mode: manifest declares granola + slack_dm, 2 pulls, 11 signals, 4 deltas (3 context applied, 1 contract gated), sweep fixes 1 stale row.

- `/mcd-sync bcaas only:slack_dm last month` → sources mode, 1 of 2 declared sources pulled.

- `/mcd-sync all slack last month` → 14 non-archived MCDs, one feed pull (30d), 23 signals routed (3 to two MCDs each), 6 MCDs touched, 4 unrouted listed, 3 links listed unfetched, one gate with 2 contract items.

- `/mcd-sync all slack only:bcaas,wally last week` → filter resolves to 2 of 14 MCDs, one feed pull (7d), signals routed only to those 2.

- `/mcd-sync outbound bcaas → DR pricing KB article` → plan: 3 updates, 1 conflict flagged; applied on approval.

- Event: `/loop bcaas …` completes → sources mode with the event payload → 2 learning nodes minted, changelog appended, no gates.

## Boundaries

- Never write MCD content directly — /mcd is the only write path

- Never run all-MCDs mode with more than one source, or sources mode against more than one MCD

- Never read a source that wasn't named or declared; never follow links without `follow-links`; never go past one hop

- Never widen a filter beyond what was named; never fall back to the default when a filter resolves to nothing

- Never select an undeclared source or an archived MCD through a filter; a bad filter name is skipped and reported, the valid remainder runs

- Never use content outside the window

- Never register a source without accepted signals, and never register DMs or bot channels

- Never silently truncate: always report when a pull hit its cap

- Never touch Archive = yes MCDs

- Never force-route an unmatched signal; never silently resolve contradictions; never cite a change without a source ref

- One gate per run; always produce a summary, changes or not; always honour dry_run

## Output

Run summary: mode · resolved sources + window · filter (e.g. only bcaas, wally — 2 of 14) · MCDs in scope / touched · deltas applied/gated/dropped · unrouted signals (all-MCDs) · ambiguities opened/resolved · contradictions · links listed/followed · integrity findings · MCD links

# MCD

Create, manage, update, and retrieve Master Context Documents per @MCD-Protocol. This is the single write/read surface for MCDs. Other skills, including `/mcd-sync`, `/loop`, `/dt-loop`, and MCD-aware agents, route MCD reads and writes through this skill rather than editing manifests or nodes directly.

The skill is optimized for Richard's preferred operating model: atomic context, explicit provenance, top-down graph traversal, surgical edits, minimal duplication, real migration rather than placeholder restructuring, and verified Notion state after structural work.

## Non-negotiable operating principles

1. **Protocol first.** Load `@MCD-Protocol` before any MCD write, migration, or structural decision. Treat it as the governing standard, not optional background reading.

1. **Inspect before mutate.** Fetch the target manifest and affected node(s) before editing. Never infer current structure from search snippets, memory, titles, or stale prior results when a fetch is available.

1. **Surgical by default.** Prefer the smallest exact edit that completes the task. Preserve unrelated wording, hierarchy, native mentions, source material, and child pages.

1. **Real migration, not empty architecture.** When refactoring an existing MCD, move/reuse substantive existing content into the new node structure. Do not create shells, summaries that replace source content, or duplicate pages merely to satisfy a template.

1. **No silent duplication.** A fact has one canonical home. Use inline mentions and routing instead of copying the same fact into multiple nodes. A resource registry records where something is, not what it says.

1. **No fabrication.** Unknown, contradictory, or unverified information becomes an ambiguity or remains explicitly unresolved. Never fill gaps with plausible prose.

1. **Top-down graph only.** `obsidian_links` is the explicit graph exception in node headers and MUST contain immediate child pages only. Never add parents, siblings, arbitrary descendants, or generic relationship metadata.

1. **Verify structural changes.** After moving, creating, nesting, splitting, or otherwise restructuring nodes, re-fetch the affected parent and child pages and confirm actual hierarchy, headers, links, and content. Do not assume a successful write means the structure is correct.

1. **Preserve history.** Never delete canonical knowledge merely because it is old. Supersede it, mark status appropriately, preserve provenance, and record the reason in the changelog where relevant.

1. **Use the existing graph before inventing a new branch.** For product MCDs, use `Systems` for substantive technical/operational structure and `FAQ & Memory` for interrogation, source-derived answers, timestamped Q&A, memory, and lifecycle context. Do not create new top-level buckets for concerns those branches already cover.

## Modes

Detect from input; if ambiguous, ask once: `Create, update, or retrieve?`

### CREATE

1. Accept a problem/opportunity statement or subject description.

1. Interrogate with up to 5 multiple-choice clarifying questions. Unanswered questions become ambiguity nodes, never blockers.

1. Load `@MCD-Protocol` and determine the profile: `product | system | project | person | business | feature`.

1. Inspect whether an MCD or relevant subject already exists before creating anything. Search is for discovery only when routing or direct lookup is insufficient.

1. Draft the minimum viable manifest and node set: manifest identity, routing, resource registry, changelog; then only the nodes required by the profile and known concerns.

1. For product MCDs, add `FAQ & Memory` as a first-class interrogation surface. Add `Systems` only when substantive technical/operational source pages or concerns exist. Never create branch placeholders just because the protocol permits them.

1. Reuse existing substantive pages where possible. If a legacy page already contains material knowledge, migrate or nest that knowledge rather than creating a second canonical copy.

1. Present the proposed structure and any consequential contract/identity changes for approval before creating or changing those gated surfaces.

1. Create the manifest and nodes in Notion. Register each actual node in the manifest. Set headers consistently and initialize `obsidian_links` only with actual immediate children.

1. Verify the resulting hierarchy and manifest routing after creation.

### UPDATE

1. Identify the target MCD and fetch its manifest first. Route from the manifest before searching.

1. Fetch only the affected node(s) and any parent/child page needed to understand the edit. Do not bulk-fetch the entire MCD without a reason.

1. Determine whether the incoming information is new, corrective, contradictory, superseding, or merely contextual.

1. Apply the smallest complete edit. Update the node body and its own `freshness`, `completeness`, and `status` header together when applicable.

1. If the concern is genuinely atomic but new, mint a new node and manifest row. Do not grow an unrelated node into a dumping ground.

1. If a node has accumulated multiple concerns or sustained internal structure, apply the promotion rule: branch it into a subject with its own manifest, and leave the original node as a concise pointer/stub.

1. Maintain `obsidian_links` as the top-down index of immediate children only. Whenever child nesting changes, update the parent's `obsidian_links` in the same structural transaction.

1. Touch manifest routing rows only when routing meaning changes: node added, renamed, retired, split, or materially changed in scope.

1. Contract-class nodes and manifest Identity require Richard's explicit approval before mutation. Context-class writes may proceed, but must produce a delta summary.

1. After any structural edit, move, split, merge, or branch change, re-fetch the relevant pages and verify actual hierarchy, child links, node headers, and preserved content.

1. Never silently trash or delete legacy source pages during cleanup. Prefer nesting, superseding, or explicit archive treatment; deletion requires a clear user instruction and preservation checks.

### GET

1. Fetch the manifest first, always.

1. Answer from the manifest if sufficient.

1. Otherwise batch-fetch the routed nodes, with a normal budget of ≤3 nodes and ≤2 hops from the manifest.

1. Follow inline mentions only when the routed nodes do not contain enough information.

1. Search Notion only when routing fails or the user explicitly asks for discovery. Treat the miss as a manifest/routing gap rather than silently normalizing search-first behavior.

1. Never let retrieval silently sprawl. If a routine question needs more than the expected retrieval budget, diagnose whether the MCD structure or routing is wrong.

1. Surface material freshness, contradictions, or unresolved ambiguity in the answer rather than presenting stale or conflicting context as canonical.

## Product branch rules

For product MCDs:

- `Systems` is for substantive architecture, product design, mechanics, requirements, schemas, infrastructure/environment, bootstrap/provisioning, and acceptance material.

- `FAQ & Memory` is for crafted FAQs, source-derived answers, timestamped Q&A, agent memory, interrogation history, and lifecycle context.

- Historical technical/source pages should be nested under the appropriate branch and retained as substantive pages when they still carry useful knowledge.

- Do not duplicate an MCD child page into `Resources` merely because it exists. The graph already provides that route.

- Use `Resources` for reusable or cross-cutting destinations that people/agents need to find: external docs, Confluence/Jira spaces, calculators, canonical documents, repositories, and stable internal source handles.

- Use `Artefacts` for concrete outputs/deliverables produced from or informed by the MCD.

- Treat `FAQ & Memory` as a knowledge lifecycle surface, not as a second generic notes bucket.

## Resource rules

Use the resource ladder from `@MCD-Protocol`: `sources:` → registry row → dedicated resource node when prose/state is needed.

A resource registry entry should identify the stable handle, destination, what it contains, and when to use it. Keep endpoints active and searchable. Do not invent URLs. If a destination is uncertain, record the source name and ambiguity rather than manufacturing a link.

## Node discipline

Every node should conform to the protocol:

```yaml
scope: [one line — what this covers and does not]
class: contract | context
freshness: [YYYY-MM-DD verified] · [YYYY-MM-DD source date]
completeness: full | partial | stub
status: active | superseded
sources: [feeds, if synced]
obsidian_links: [immediate child pages only]
```

Node types are `intent | constraint | decision | stakeholder | customer | contract | ambiguity | learning | resource`. Learning nodes must identify `pattern` or `anti-pattern` in their first line. One node = one concern.

## Approval and integrity gates

- Never write before loading `@MCD-Protocol`.

- Never mutate `class: contract` or manifest Identity without Richard's approval.

- Never create a duplicate canonical node when an existing node already owns the concern.

- Never create a placeholder page purely to satisfy the expected template.

- Never broad-replace a large manifest or node when a targeted edit will do.

- Never move or rename a page based only on title similarity; fetch and confirm identity/content first.

- Never assume a move succeeded because the tool returned success. Verify parentage with a fetch.

- When restructuring a manifest via `replace_content`, include `<page url="...">` tags for every existing child page that must survive (the operation refuses and lists them otherwise), and re-check the page's title/`Name` property in the same verification pass — `replace_content` has been observed to silently corrupt the title alongside content, and Step 8's hierarchy/content check alone will miss that.

- Never delete a child page during replacement without an explicit instruction to delete it and a visible preservation/deletion check.

- Never use search as the default retrieval path when manifest routing exists.

- Never copy historical facts into current canonical nodes without resolving their status or provenance.

- Never conceal structural uncertainty. Report it and preserve the existing source until the hierarchy is proven.

## Retrieval integrity

When sources conflict:

1. Prefer the current canonical node and explicitly recorded decisions over legacy copies.

1. Prefer the authoritative source endpoint when the MCD identifies one.

1. Use freshness as a contextual signal, not proof of authority.

1. If the conflict cannot be resolved, preserve both histories and mint/update an ambiguity node.

1. Do not silently collapse materially different values into one “best guess”.

## Examples

- `/mcd create — new project: EaaS escrow automation for tier-2 banks` → inspect for an existing subject, ask up to 5 MC questions, create the project profile plus intent/resource/ambiguity nodes actually needed, and verify the hierarchy.

- `/mcd what constraints apply to BCaaS DR pricing?` → GET: manifest → relevant constraint/contract nodes → answer with freshness/ambiguity flags.

- `/mcd update — Tiago confirmed the 4-tier model is final` → route to the relevant decision/contract context, fetch existing nodes first, mint or update the decision as appropriate, mark superseded history, update routing only if needed, and gate contract mutation for approval.

- `/mcd refactor this legacy product MCD` → audit existing substantive pages first, define the new graph, migrate content into atomic nodes and branches, preserve source pages/history, update parent `obsidian_links`, and verify the final hierarchy. Do not replace rich pages with empty stubs or duplicate the same content across branches.

## Output

- CREATE: manifest URL + actual node list + open ambiguities + structural verification note

- UPDATE: delta summary with nodes touched, rows changed, superseded items, approvals/gates, and verification result

- GET: the answer, with routed node links and freshness/ambiguity flags where material

## Boundaries

- `/mcd` is the only MCD write/read surface.

- `/mcd-sync` may discover integrity deltas, but it must route actual MCD writes through `/mcd`.

- `/manage-spec` and `/reconcile-spec` are superseded for MCD operations.
